Details: Every feature for date t may use only information timestamped <= 18:00 ET on trading day t.
Snapshot raw downloads daily with a retrieval timestamp; build history from snapshots or vintage-aware APIs (ALFRED realtime_start/realtime_end) rather than today's revised data.
FRED daily series: lag 1 business day by default. DTWEXBGS: weekly release, lag up to ~1 week. Monthly macro: usable only from release date (8:30 a.m. ET) onward, then forward-fill.
Use first-release (or as-of-t vintage) values for payrolls, PCE, seasonally adjusted CPI. Never use final revised history in backtests.
Adjust prices and volumes for splits using only split events with ex-date <= t when reconstructing history; dollar volume and returns are split-invariant. Verify adjustment factors after each split.
Use total-return (dividend-adjusted) closes for ETFs with distributions; adjustment for a dividend applies from its ex-date.
Align all series on the equity trading calendar (src 25). Forward-fill non-equity series (bond-market holidays, weekends for crypto) with a staleness counter; never back-fill.
Label uses close_{t+1} of the next trading session; drop final row; features never include any t+1 field.
Use official end-of-day values. Verify put/call statistics are posted before 18:00 ET historically; if not, lag 1 day.
Par yield curve posting is close to the 18:00 cutoff; default to t-1 values unless posting time is verified.
Sample BTC/ETH at exactly 18:00 ET from hourly/minute candles; do not use UTC daily candles (close after cutoff). Handle DST shifts.
Use acceptanceDateTime (ET), not filingDate. Window for day t = (18:00 ET t-1, 18:00 ET t].
Only scheduled events known at t (FOMC, BLS, holidays, OPEX) may be forward-looking. Earnings dates must be estimated or taken from announcements made before t.
All z-scores, betas, SMAs, scalers use trailing windows ending at t; discard warm-up rows; fit any normalization inside each training fold only.
Use only instruments trading at t (e.g. ARM after IPO). Handle tickers renamed (e.g. META formerly FB) by mapping history correctly.
Represent missing as NaN plus a missing-indicator; never fill with future values or full-sample means.
Flag early-close days; their volume/range features are not comparable to full sessions.
z-scaled moves divide today's change by the stdev of that change over the trailing 60 observations ending t-1 (exclude today). Require a minimum number of valid observations; NaN otherwise.

'Days to' features may use only dates known in advance at t (published schedules, announced dates). Unknown/unscheduled events (intermeeting FOMC, unannounced earnings) must never appear before they are announced; use estimates explicitly flagged as estimates.
Derived dates (e.g. FOMC minutes = decision + 21 calendar days, estimated NVDA earnings) are flagged 'derived'; replace with the official date only from the time it was published.
Count in trading days, cap at a fixed maximum, and set NaN during burn-in before the first event is observed (do not assume an event happened just before the sample).
Fixed thresholds (5% move, VIX 30, Form 4 cluster size) are set a priori or chosen inside training folds only; percentile thresholds use trailing windows.
For lagged series (FRED, Treasury default), changes are computed on the lagged values (e.g. t-1 vs t-2), not mixing a same-day value with a lagged one.
Sources marked 'proposed / not in inventory' (BEA schedule, peer/hyperscaler earnings, NVIDIA events, index rebalances) need their own point-in-time archive before use.
